profile.name: Jhelianne Figuerres
profile.tagline: I build interfaces that behave, and design ones that feel considered.
profile.bio: I'm an IT student at Lorma Colleges, splitting my time between frontend development, UI/UX design, and Java programming. I like projects that have a real story behind them — a shop, a system, a person using it — rather than throwaway demos. Most of what's below started as a class requirement and turned into something I kept iterating on.

projects.title: The Crafter's Loop
projects.description: A crochet & yarn e-commerce concept, taken from a horizontally scrolling products page all the way through a full Figma prototype documented in a 29-figure research paper.

projects.title: Personal Portfolio (this site)
projects.description: A responsive, JSON-driven portfolio built mobile-first, with dynamic rendering so new projects and skills never require touching the HTML.

projects.title: JF Core Systems
projects.description: A multi-module Java application bundling a mini-mart POS, a movie rental system, a clothing registration system, and a trivia game, using Gson for JSON persistence.

projects.title: Networked Client-Server POS
projects.description: A multithreaded point-of-sale system with a dedicated server, client handler, and file manager, using inheritance to model accounts and synchronized file writes.

timeline.title: Tertiary
timeline.description: Coursework spanning frontend web development, UI/UX design, and Java programming, alongside general education subjects.

timeline.title: Secondary
timeline.place: Castor Z. Concepcion Memorial National High School
timeline.description: Completed junior and senior high school under the STEM strand, where a strong grounding in math and science built the analytical habits I now bring to programming and design.

timeline.title: Primary
timeline.description: Completed elementary schooling, building the foundation in reading, math, and basic computer literacy that first got me curious about how software works.
